03 / A SECOND PARAGRAPH

A footnote,
who doesn't want to finish.

Anna can't get anywhere. Her colleague Mira knows the tradition.

Anna has changed her explanation several times. It sounds plausible. But an allusion doesn't quite fit yet. Mira offers to look at the passage. The edition does not have to be finished: A clearly marked version and a short introduction to the edition principles are sufficient for this test order.

A question becomes a different interpretation.

Mira finds a parallel passage. Anna checks the note and revises the comment. She notes why she has changed her explanation and names Mira's contribution. The earlier version remains comparable in the protected working process.

The exchange is a gain and takes time: Anna has to give context, answer questions and decide on integration. Mira needs an understandable section and a matching return channel for this.

CONSTRUCTION 1 · BEFORE READING

A wider concept

"Neighbours came to help." The commentary points out that "neighbors" first of all as a general term for people from the surrounding area. Whether the term bears a more precise social classification remains open. Anna therefore considers a broad explanation appropriate without naming a single group. This uncertainty should be recognizable for readers: inside; further evidence from the relationship between tradition is still pending at this point in time.

CONSTRUCTION 2 · BY MIRAS NOTE

A well-founded clarification

"Neighbors came to help. A supplementary evidence suggests in the fictitious example that the term refers to a local community. Anna examines the context and explains the narrower reading in the commentary. The previous general interpretation is documented as an earlier assumption. Mira's note is explicitly mentioned; Anna takes over the technical decision on the new declaration and its limits.

Amended: the interpretation of an expression. Reason: additional contextual evidence. Contribution: Mira's note, Anna's examination. Git makes versions comparable; the reason comes from the edition work.

A CONCLUSION ON THE RAND

"This sentence needs a coffee."

Anna and Mira are now in a lively exchange. As they used to write word comments, they write queries directly to the passage, this time as XML comments. Not every sentence is ready for printing: Between an exact observation and an open question there is also once a small Kalauer.

<!-- Mira: This sentence needs a coffee. Me too. Do you really mean the whole neighborhood? -->
<!-- Anna: First coffee, then context! I'll look at your receipt. Thanks for reading back. -->

Freely invented example. XML comments belong here to internal communication, not to the scientific commentaries.

The comment's deleted.

Before the approval, Anna removes the internal notes. In the current TEI file, only the scientifically tested version can be seen. But once the notes have been saved in a commit, they can be read more in older Git stands. Deletion in a new version does not remove them retroactively.

What someone could find in an older Git version
<!-- Mira: This set needs coffee. Me too. -->

When Anna makes the same working repository public, his achievable history can also publish the internal conversation. Private contributors also see only what they should actually have access to: The reading circle must be consciously defined.

Anna wants to keep the helpful collaboration and yet present a clean publication. Therefore, she separates the private working repository from her own publication repository. There she takes over audited, cleaned files without the private Git history. Mira's scientific contribution is expressly appreciated.

What should Anna publish – and where?

How much access does Mira need?

A test export can be enough. It doesn't need to see all the work notes. Discover below how approval and support costs change.

05

THE LOCATION
EXCHANGES

THE EDITION CAN COME

A repo can be used
move.

Anna learns that her university access will run out. That's annoying – but her edition work is not tied to this server.

Git holds the versioned files and their history in Anna's complete local copy. She can transfer them to another suitable work place. To do this, she needs an understandable guide, a new access and time to check.

The move of the repos doesn't solve every question at the same time. Maybe their oXygen permission also ends, maybe consultation remains possible. Another XML tool can edit the same TEI data; the usual work interface and tests must then be set up appropriately. Anna clarifies these things separately.

Repo removal: a guide for Anna
  1. Check before the old end of access. In the Git client, get the last levels from the Uni-Repo. Check, commit and transfer your own changes. Get the full local Git copy; a ZIP download of the current files does not contain the history.
  2. Preparing a new place of work. Select access and create an empty, initially private repo there. If available, a suitable import function of the target host can also be used.
  3. Enter a new target. In the Git client place the address of the new repos as an additional remote target. The old target remains until the successful check.
  4. Transfer files and Git history. Push the main branch and existing tags to the new goal; explicitly include other industries needed. Anna's routine does not need a new project architecture for this.
  5. Really try the copy. Clone the new repo into a fresh folder. Compare file version, previous commits and tags; perform validation and preview. Check for large externally stored objects and subprojects to see if they have come with them completely.
  6. Documenting new work place. Write down the destination address, date and test result. Then change the daily comparison to the new target. If available, transfer issues, access rights, automatic processes and web publication separately or set up a new one.

For the small repo with text files and few additional functions, this is a well-writable process that Anna herself can carry out. Direct technical assistance is needed especially in special cases – such as a complex pipeline. official Git manual for remote repositories.

Anna can test the change in advance in peace. Then an imminent end of access remains a manageable task. At the same time, a useful guide and proof are created that her project can continue to work elsewhere.

06 / THE CONTINUES HIS READER TEXT

A book would be nice.
The data may:
already out.

Anna dreams of inspiring a publisher for her edition, but she doesn't want to have to wait until her work benefits others.

A carefully designed book, perhaps with a helpful reviewer and a publisher who reaches the right readers: inside: that would be a great opportunity. Anna remains realistic. For her small topic a publishing contract is not secure. Tested TEI data and if necessary a simple reading view on the web are for her a meaningful independent publication path.

Both can fit together. A book could record a certain edition status; the digital edition could later incorporate new insights. Anna needs to clarify early on which rights, services, costs and version rules are agreed.

THREE WAGES FOR DATAPUBLICATION

What exactly makes Anna public?

Release the same working repository?

Technically, the path is short: Anna changes the reading circle of the repos. But this also allows to access previous file versions, old XML comments and metadata. It is not enough to clean up the current file. All accessible public content and history must be checked appropriately.

For Anna and Mira's flabby work talks this is the unfavorable standard way. A mere public additional work branch also does not reliably protect private history.

A separate publication repository: Anna's preferred way

The working repo remains private. Anna selects a shareable version and exports the required TEI files. She removes internal XML comments and also checks metadata, file names and accompanying files. She does not take over the private Git folder or work history.

The new public repo initially contains only the verified data, a README, edition principles, contributions and responsibilities, terms of use and version information. It carries its own history of the published stands. A clone of the working repositorys with subsequent deletion of the comments would not be such a separation.

Before each new approval, Anna checks the export and a fresh public copy. An appropriate archive transfer and persistent identifier is also agreed; a public repo alone does not guarantee long-term preservation.

A small website – for example with GitHub Pages?

Many readers want to read text and comment without downloading TEI files. A minimal frontend can offer a home page, a simple text view with job comments, download links and a quote note. A large edition database is not necessary for this.

What is GitHub Pages? A publishing service from GitHub: It turns the website files of a repos into a website with its own web address. Anna does not need a self-run web server for this. "Statistical" means: The pages consist of HTML, CSS and if necessary JavaScript; an own database or server-side application does not belong to it. Interactive functions in the browser are nevertheless possible.

For Anna, this could mean: your verified TEI data will be transformed into a simple read view with comment and download. GitHub Pages provides this website. As the TEI markup is displayed, a suitable template or a small program must be set beforehand. Anna also updates the resulting website for new editions.

The publication repository may contain released TEI data and the related website; a third repo is not automatically required. Anna can continue to work privately in the working repo on Uni-GitLab. Available functions, account and publication conditions must be checked at setup.

Uni-Website, own website or GitHub Pages?

Anna could also accommodate her edition on the university website. To do this, she must first win people: Why does the project belong there? Who sets up the reading view, can record new stands and take care of them after Anna's retirement? Design specifications and technical possibilities have to fit into the output path. If there is already a suitable edition service, this way can make much easier. Otherwise, Anna needs time for reasoning, coordination and technical support.

A self-organized website gives Anna more room for design. It also binds the project to another permanent task: hosting and possibly paying domain, managing accesses, organizing updates and backup, responding to faults and finding a representation. How much expertise is needed depends on the solution; a maintained static offer is more manageable than a self-maintained editorial system. Nevertheless, it must be clear who takes care of himself in the long term.

Why for Anna GitHub Pages? For a small static edition view, it can be a simple choice that is appropriate to the purpose: The checked website files are at the publication repository, GitHub takes over their deployment. Anna does not have to operate its own web server and negotiate no inclusion into the university website. Setting up, TEI output, checking and later updating remain tasks. A separate web address would also be combinable with GitHab Pages; web address and hosting are separate decisions.

Anna therefore keeps the output path as transferable as possible: TEI data, website files and instructions remain available. Thus, the edition can later also switch to a suitable university service or another provider. The choice of GitHub Pages is a pragmatic project decision, not a commitment to permanent archiving.

Developing a small front end with AI?

Anna has an idea: "Links to the letter text, next to the comment – and please have a button for downloading." With an AI programming assistant, she can gradually develop a first website. Vibe Coding called: Describe wishes in everyday language, try out a design and continue working together with the AI. For a manageable prototype this can make it easier to get started.

Anna starts with a small TEI example suitable for passing on and clear rules: How should additions, deletions, uncertain readings and notes appear? She compares the output with the source data, even in difficult places, and checks operation by keyboard and mobile phone. A pretty design is only a usable edition view when the editorial statements are correct. An existing TEI output template can serve as a starting point.

How does Git help? Anna holds up working intermediates and can compare or remove changes. For later maintenance, she also keeps the output rules and a short guide in addition to the frontend: How does a new TEI-version turn into a website again? Before the approval, she lets the output path technically and if necessary read back.

REQUIREMENTS AND DATA SUMMARY

What wins Anna – and what remains mobile?

QuestionPublishing bookTEI data / small website
What could it offer?Editing, design and appropriate distribution, if actually agreed.Early provision, reusable data and a accessible reading stand even without publishing houses.
How much work?voting, correction of rates, time and, where appropriate, financial contributions.Release testing, documentation, setup and maintenance of a manageable offer.
What needs to be clarified?Rights to text, comment, images and sentence; existing and planned open versions; later revisions.Own and third-party rights, appropriate license, carrier and receipt. Consider already granted usage rights.
What happens with new insights?Existing print copies remain unchanged. Errata or new edition need their own way.Anna can publish a new reviewed version and explain changes; the older cited version remains identifiable.

Anna records the data status of the book edition. Later digital versions mark it as revisions and explain the differences. A mere file comparison does not replace her edition report.

Open data and a later publishing contract

Before an agreement is reached, Anna clarifies which edition and which components of a contract concerns: the TEI data, the commentary, illustrations, the web view or only the set book version. She discloses existing publications and licenses and explicitly asks for further data access and revision options.

An effectively issued CC license cannot be simply withdrawn from users: those who comply with their terms and conditions. At the same time, a CC license is not exclusive; additional agreements are in principle possible. What a publisher can offer and how this fits into Anna's rights has to be clarified in concrete terms. The book is thus neither excluded nor secured without further examination.
